artifact_purpose: The declared half of the R02 operator review: for every observation of the ESR record, whether the evidence the comparison resolved supports the proposition the ESR states, what the ESR complains of, the uncertainty that remains, the recommendation and the decision the operator has to take. Resolution of a reference is measured by harness/operator_review.py; agreement is judged here. The two are deliberately separate fields: a finding can resolve perfectly and still be about something else.
declared_by: drafted in a Claude Code session, 2026-10-07; every row is a provisional reading for operator review and none records an operator decision
declared_status_note: declared_status is the status of the agreement judgment itself (CLAUDE.md §12.2): Inferred where it follows from the resolved findings and the verified quotes, Assumed where it rests on a reading of intent, Unresolved where this copy cannot settle it.
vocabulary_note: semantic_agreement: agreed, disputed, unresolved, not_applicable (no finding to compare). esr_complaint: absent_detail, inadequately_explained, both, other, not_applicable. recommendation: retain, revisit_in_r03, revisit_after_declaration, revisit_after_private_network. No disposition is changed here; a recommended change is a question, not an act.

rows.agreement_basis: Three criterion strengths name the four-pillar architecture linking O1-O4 and the nine individually specified DC projects, which are the two things the ESR praises. The exc-obj cell passes 3/3. No finding contests the objectives.

Two criterion strengths name the closed-loop pipeline and the integration of computer science, clinical, regulatory and social science across work packages. That is the ESR's 'methodology clearly described' and 'interdisciplinary approaches coherent'. The exc-method cell is the report's highest at 0.79.
All five criterion samples fault the causal-AI methodology for naming no techniques, estimators or validation metrics. That is the first clause of the ESR sentence, word for word in substance.
rows.uncertainty: This observation and ESR-E-02 carry the same ESR sentence: the operator's transcription split one sentence into its AI/ML clause and its security clause. The blind lane covers the first clause only, so the sentence counts once as detected and once as missed. Every other observation has text of its own.
rows.operator_decision: Confirm that splitting one ESR sentence into ESR-E-01 and ESR-E-02 is intended. It is the only such split, and it puts one sentence on both sides of the detection count.

rows.agreement_basis: No blind sample, cell rationale or audit check names security of clinical data, so there is no finding whose proposition could agree or disagree. The copy carries two passing references to data protection and no security passage.
rows.uncertainty: The disposition counts this as a miss on the ground that the ESR itself found the submission thin, so the copy cannot be thinner in kind. That is a reading of the ESR's wording, not a measurement: the register records prose 'some passages omitted or rephrased', so a security passage may have been removed. The preservation status is declared Assumed.
rows.operator_decision: Decide whether a miss may be counted against the lane on Assumed preservation. If the R04 declaration for 1.2 cannot say the security content is no thinner than the submission's, this row belongs in 'partially observable' or 'not assessable'.

rows.agreement_basis: No finding raises the retrospective-only evaluation design. The three quoted passages establish that the copy states retrospective evaluation in the objectives, in Task 4.3 and in the state-of-the-art section.
rows.uncertainty: The copy does say the case studies 'progress from retrospective analyses toward shadow-mode and implementation-oriented evaluations'. The ESR's point is that the prospective plans are limited, which is a judgment of degree. A lane that read the shadow-mode sentence as a prospective plan is not plainly wrong, so whether this is a blindness or a difference of degree is unsettled.
rows.operator_decision: Decide whether a judgment of degree — 'limited plans for prospective validation' against a stated shadow-mode progression — counts as a point the lane should have raised.

rows.agreement_basis: The one cited finding says feasibility details such as sample sizes, data access timelines and power considerations are not specified for the clinical cohorts. The ESR's point is a multihospital, multi-operator design reflecting contemporary European TAVI practice. Sample size and site or operator diversity are different properties of a cohort, and no finding names the second.
rows.uncertainty: Task 4.3 says 'multicentre' and lists data sources, with no site count, operator count or cohort size. The register records prose omitted or rephrased, so whether the submission said more about the cohort is not measurable from this copy.
rows.operator_decision: Decide whether 'sample sizes not specified' and 'multihospital, multi-operator design' are the same proposition. If they are not, the partial detection rests on no finding and the row is a miss or not assessable.

rows.agreement_basis: No finding names the database or its contributing clinicians, and the word does not occur in the copy's Part B. There is nothing in this copy for a finding to be about.
rows.uncertainty: Two causes of the absence cannot be told apart here: the referent was generalised away with the identifiers, or the submission introduced the database in a passage the register records as omitted. The disposition's 'not assessable from this copy' is the honest reading either way, and it is the only such row of the 29.
rows.operator_decision: Confirm against the submitted original whether a registry or database passage with contributing clinicians existed, and whether sanitisation removed it. Until then this row carries no verdict on the lane.

rows.agreement_basis: All five samples fault the gender and diversity dimension for being stated as a principle without operational links to the specific cohorts and datasets. That is the ESR's complaint that the consideration is not detailed enough for clinical issues in cardiology, and the cohorts in question are the cardiology cohorts.

The ESR credits open science practices 'such as preprints, and repositories', which means the submission named them. Three samples fault the commitments for naming no repositories, licences or governance. The two readings cannot both describe the same text.
rows.uncertainty: The register records identifiers generalised and every citation removed. Named repositories and venues are the kind of content that sanitisation strips, so the contest may rest on evidence this copy lacks rather than on a weakness of the proposal.
rows.operator_decision: Confirm whether the submission named repositories and preprint venues under 1.2. If it did, the blind contest is a sanitisation artifact and must not enter the revision plan as a weakness.

rows.agreement_basis: Three criterion strengths name the TG1-TG6 mapping, the Personal Career Development Plans and the table of network-wide events, and the exc-training cell passes 3/3. That is the ESR's solid training framework with meaningful network-wide events.
No finding faults the depth of the local-training description. The quoted passages show the paragraph survives under 1.3.
rows.uncertainty: The exc-training cell members cite the same paragraph approvingly, as complementarity explicitly stated. The lane therefore read the passage the evaluators read and judged it sufficient. That is a disagreement of degree rather than a failure to see the passage, and the detection rate does not distinguish the two.
rows.operator_decision: Decide whether a passage the lane read and cited as a strength can be counted as a missed criticism. Three of the six alleged misses (ESR-E-07, ESR-E-09, ESR-Q-02) have this shape.

rows.agreement_basis: No blind sample and no cell rationale names entrepreneurship. The quoted passages show the TG5 goal and the 2.2 sentence survive, and neither says how a fellow applies the training.
rows.uncertainty: The missing thing is a mechanism, which is an absence the lane could have named from this copy. The preservation status is Assumed, as for every miss.
rows.operator_decision: Confirm in the R04 declaration for 1.3 and 2.2 that the entrepreneurship passages are preserved. On that confirmation this row is the cleanest of the six misses.

rows.agreement_basis: The supervision structure the ESR calls well-structured and multi-layered is named as a strength in every sample, so that half agrees. The supervisors' experience is contested by three samples and by a failing cell member, which the ESR calls experienced and highly qualified.
rows.uncertainty: Two of the contesting findings fault the anonymisation itself ('Supervisor A-K', no DC mapping), which is sanitisation and not a property of the submission. One faults H-index figures that did survive into this copy, so that part of the contest is readable here; whether those figures are the submission's own is a register question, since prose was omitted or rephrased.
rows.operator_decision: Confirm the supervisor track-record figures in this copy are the submission's. Then decide whether the uneven-track-record finding is a point the evaluators did not make, or an artifact of reading anonymised profiles.

rows.agreement_basis: No sample asks how supervisory quality is measured. The one sentence that answers it survives in 1.4 and is quoted.
rows.uncertainty: The exc-supervision cell members cite that sentence as a strength, naming the feedback questionnaires. As with ESR-E-07, the lane read the passage and judged it adequate where the evaluators called it generic.
rows.operator_decision: Decide, with ESR-E-07, whether a degree disagreement over a passage the lane cited approvingly counts as a miss.

rows.agreement_basis: Three criterion strengths name the structured secondments, the non-academic co-supervision and the Supervisory Board and ITP roles, and the imp-structuring cell passes 3/3. Those are the ESR's own examples.
rows.uncertainty: Two samples add an arithmetic contradiction the evaluators did not record: section 2.1 claims at least 80% of secondment months in non-academic settings, while the DC table sums to about 74% and DC7 shows ten secondment months with none non-academic. That is computed from the appendix table as this copy carries it.
rows.operator_decision: Confirm the appendix secondment months in this copy are the submission's. If they are, decide whether the 80% contradiction enters the R05 revision plan as a correction the ESR did not ask for.

rows.agreement_basis: Three criterion strengths name the knowledge hub, the ECTS integration, the alumni hub and the Innovation and Sustainability Committee. The ESR names the virtual knowledge hub and the sustained long-term collaboration.
rows.uncertainty: Two samples fault the post-project funding plan as a list of programme names. The ESR does not fault it. The finding is about a different sentence of 2.1 than the praise rests on.
rows.operator_decision: Decide whether the post-project funding plan is revised in R05 even though the ESR praised this aspect. A revision here is an improvement beyond the ESR, not a response to it.

rows.agreement_basis: Three criterion strengths name the PCDP within three months, the multi-mentor PhD committee and the differentiated career pathways, and the imp-career cell passes 3/3 at 0.78. No sample contests the career measures.

The ESR credits clear objectives, measurable indicators and clearly identified target groups. Four samples fault the communication plan for having no audience segmentation and no communication indicators, and the imp-dissemination cell fails 2 of 3. The readings contradict each other on the same sub-section.
rows.uncertainty: The register measures zero images on any page and records every figure lost. A dissemination table or figure of target groups and indicators is exactly what that loss removes, so the cell failure may be an artifact of the copy.
rows.operator_decision: Confirm whether 2.3 carried a target-group or indicator table or figure in the submission. The failing cell is the only one of three in impact, so this answer changes how the impact score difference is read.

rows.agreement_basis: Three samples say the IP strategy restates Horizon Europe boilerplate without naming which results are protectable or how. That is the ESR's finding that strategies to protect industrial outcomes are not convincingly elaborated. The quoted passages are the generic commitments the findings describe.

Two criterion strengths credit the scientific, economic and societal pathways as distinct and coherent, which is the ESR's 'highly credible' and 'well-justified'. The cross-site transportability indicator the ESR names survives in the copy.
rows.uncertainty: Two samples contest the societal half: no evaluation mechanism ties training outputs to health-system outcomes, and the societal claims carry no endpoints. The ESR praises the societal justification, so the contest and the praise are about the same passage.
rows.operator_decision: Decide whether the societal-impact indicator gap enters the R05 revision plan. ESR-I-02 already asks for magnitude on the economic and technological pathways; extending it to the societal pathway goes beyond the ESR.

rows.agreement_basis: Every sample and all three imp-magnitude cell members say the magnitude of impact is stated qualitatively with no quantified targets, baselines or comparators. The cell is the report's lowest at 0.48 and uncovered. The ESR's finding is the same, limited to the economic and technological pathways.

Four criterion strengths name the seven work packages with objectives, tasks, leads and DCs, and the deliverables and milestones tables with their verification means. The impl-workplan cell passes 3/3 at 0.78. That is the ESR's work plan of good quality with coherent allocation.

Two of the three cited findings carry the ESR's point: inter-WP dependencies and critical-path logic are not mapped beyond narrative cross-references, and no dependency diagram is shown. The third says all work packages run uniformly M1-M36 'with no intermediate milestones' shown, which the copy's own milestones table contradicts: it lists months per milestone, M4.2 at M24 among them.
rows.uncertainty: The register measures zero images on any page and zero occurrences of 'dependenc', 'Gantt' and 'critical path'. A Gantt or dependency figure in the submission would have been lost, so the lane may be reporting an absence that sanitisation created rather than one the evaluators saw.
rows.operator_decision: Decide whether the 'no intermediate milestones' sentence may be cited as evidence of detection when the copy carries a milestones table with months. The dependency point stands on the other two findings either way; the citation is what is in question.

rows.agreement_basis: No sample or cell asks how deliverables are validated, and the audit's deliverable check tests windows rather than validation. The quoted table header shows the deliverables table carries no validation or acceptance column, while the milestones table does carry means of verification.
rows.uncertainty: Every sample praises the same deliverables table the ESR criticises. As with ESR-E-07 and ESR-E-09, the lane read the artifact and judged it complete.
rows.operator_decision: Decide whether a missing column in a table the lane praised in every sample is a miss. The absence is readable from this copy, which is why the row is counted against the lane today.

rows.agreement_basis: The audit finds M7.3 due at M48 while its related WP7 runs M1-M36, and that M7.3 and M4.2 name no deliverable they depend on. The ESR's point is that the definitions and timing of some milestones are not well aligned with the overall proposal. A window violation and a misalignment with the proposal are not the same proposition: a follow-up proposal submitted after the funded period may be an intentional commitment rather than a scheduling error.
rows.uncertainty: The dispositions quote no project duration, so whether M48 lies outside the project is not established in the comparison. The second audit finding rests on a rule that a milestone must name a deliverable it depends on; whether that is a sourced requirement, an inferred relationship or a drafting preference is not stated. The blind finding cited beside the audit is the same sentence disputed under ESR-Q-01.
rows.operator_decision: Establish the duration the copy states, then decide whether a follow-up-proposal milestone after the funded period is a misalignment or an intentional commitment. Decide separately whether 'names no deliverable it depends on' is a sourced requirement. Both lanes are credited with this row today.

rows.agreement_basis: Three samples say several mitigations are generic and carry no quantitative thresholds or named contingency owners. That is the ESR's finding. The quoted passages are the generic mitigation and the one risk that does state a 60% trigger.

The infrastructure-to-WP mapping and the three-axis complementarity argument the ESR praises are named as strengths in every sample, and the impl-participants cell passes 3/3. Three samples contest the capacity claims as generic institutional boilerplate without track record, which the ESR calls high-quality infrastructure and capacity.
rows.uncertainty: The register records identifiers generalised, and section 8 reaches this copy as unnamed 'Academic Beneficiary A-I' profiles across 28,087 characters. Prior grants, named facilities and publication records are what that generalisation removes.
rows.operator_decision: Confirm whether section 8 carried track-record evidence in the submission. If it did, the three contesting findings describe the sanitisation and not the proposal.

rows.agreement_basis: Four samples call the hosting arrangements generic, a single sentence on accredited doctoral schools and international offices. The ESR calls the same arrangements credible and supportive. One cell member reads the per-beneficiary profiles as tying named infrastructure to work packages.
rows.uncertainty: Section 5, the network organisation, reaches this copy as 3,135 characters with identifiers generalised. Per-institution hosting detail the evaluators may have read there does not reach this copy, and the contest cannot be reconciled with the praise from what remains.
rows.operator_decision: Confirm what section 5 carried in the submission. Then decide whether four findings against a point the evaluators called credible count as a lane disagreement or as a reading of a shortened section.

rows.agreement_basis: Four criterion strengths name the associated partners' differentiated roles as industrial secondment hosts, causal-AI co-supervision and external cohort providers. That is the ESR's 'roles of all associated partners are described in detail'. The one nuance a sample adds, that their infrastructure is less detailed than the beneficiaries', is not an ESR point.
